Subject: Quick sync: renewal coming up (usage + perf questions)

Hi Avery,

Hope you had a great holiday — our renewal for BH-2219 is coming up end of January and the execs want a short health review before the contract discussion. Two things we'd like to cover:

1) Our token spend spiked in December (~30M tokens) vs our run-rate (18M). We need to understand if this is sustainable or a transient burst.
2) We're seeing a 20% latency regression on the image-captioning pipelines when traffic peaks (p95 up ~200ms). We need guidance on whether switching to a dedicated reservation or tuning batching/quantization will meaningfully reduce costs without impacting quality.

Can we get a concise usage & ROI recap and a proposed term/commit option that keeps latency under 300ms p95 while not doubling our spend? A 30–45 minute call next week would be ideal.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Lee
Head of ML Infrastructure, BlueHarvest

Team — forwarding Sam's note and the billing CSV. Quick alignment before the call next week:

Ask: produce a compact renewal playbook we can share in the 1/13 customer meeting. Must include:
- Short usage analysis (burst vs baseline) and recommended commit sizing for next 12 months (targeting <10% spend increase vs baseline, while accommodating expected growth).
- Two term options: (A) conservative: 12-month reserved capacity + 10% headroom; (B) aggressive: 18-month commit with pre-negotiated burst lanes and reduced per-token price.
- Ops actions: caching + batching knobs, a quick quantization pilot (1 week) and expected token-cost delta for each.
- SLA/loss-of-service fallback (how we handle region failover / model fallback).

Ben: can you draft pricing for both options and attach a short model-cost worksheet?
Marissa: please prepare a one-pager on the pilot runbook (owner, timeline, measurable success criteria).
Karthik: any specific perf knobs / recommended quantization profiles you want called out?

Target: internal deck by 1/8 EOD so we can iterate.

Thanks — Avery

Subject: RE: BlueHarvest renewal: usage health, scaling options and proposed terms

Avery / Marissa — draft numbers attached (see BH-renewal-proposal-Q1-2027.pdf and latency-and-cost-benchmarks.xlsx). Key assumptions below:

- Baseline run-rate (ex-burst): 18M tokens/month. December spike: 30M (one-off end-of-year batch jobs we suspect).
- Option A (12m reserved): commit 22M tokens/mo, includes 10% burst credit. Expected monthly bill ~ $14.2k (net of discounts) -> ~+6% YoY spend vs baseline.
- Option B (18m commit with burst lanes): commit 24M tokens/mo with on-demand burst up to 40M at pre-negotiated unit price; expected monthly bill ~$16.8k but includes priority capacity and lower per-token cost on sustained usage.

Cost reduction levers modeled:
- Quantization pilot (INT8-ish profile): ~22% token $ reduction for captioning models, validated on sample workloads.
- Batching + caching: additional ~12% effective token savings under steady-state traffic.

Net: if BlueHarvest runs the quantization pilot + apply batching/caching, effective spend under Option B could be similar to their current baseline while giving them the headroom for peak traffic and better latency SLOs (~p95 < 300ms in dedicated lane).

Attachments: BH-renewal-proposal-Q1-2027.pdf (proposal + price table), latency-and-cost-benchmarks.xlsx (detailed model/perf sims).

I'll be on the 1/13 call.
Ben
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Hi Sam / Priya — thanks for the call today. Linking the short TL;DR and attachments we promised.

TL;DR:
- December was a one-time batch/retargeting spike (30M tokens). Baseline run-rate is 18M tokens/month.
- Proposed commercial options:
  • Option A (12mo): reserve 22M tokens/mo (+10% headroom). Lower near-term commitment; modest price improvement.
  • Option B (18mo + burst lanes): reserve 24M tokens/mo, pre-negotiated burst to 40M. Better per-token economics and priority capacity for peak windows.
- Ops & cost-savings package (pilot):
  • 1-week quantization pilot on captioning model (expected ~22% token $ reduction)
  • Batching/caching recommendations (expected ~12% additional savings)
  • Combined: projected effective spend near current baseline while delivering p95 latency <300ms in the dedicated lane.

Attachments (same as discussed): blueharvest-monthly-usage-2026-12.csv, BH-renewal-proposal-Q1-2027.pdf, latency-and-cost-benchmarks.xlsx

Next steps:
1) BlueHarvest: confirm preferred commercial option (A or B) and whether you want the quantization pilot to run the week of Jan 24.
2) If you pick Option B, we'll issue a draft addendum and DocuSign link for review within 48 hours.
3) Both sides: schedule a 30-minute pilot kickoff (ops + engineering) if pilot approved.

If you'd like, I can circulate a 1-page comparison table by EOD Wed.

Thanks again — appreciate the constructive discussion.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
